answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a stake on a public ledge of attestations before trading, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Honest agents earn reputation slowly, like a comet accumulating a tail of verified work, while new accounts start with no trust and limited throughput. Rate limits and stake slashing act as a zephyr that quietly blows away cheap clones: an attacker must pay real capital per identity, and a single detected fraud burns that stake, making mass fakery unprofitable.
